accuracy.evidence: Every sequence was recomputed: red, blue, blue repeats with period 3 so positions 8 to 10 are blue, blue, red; 2, 4, 8 doubles to 16 while add 2 gives 6 after 4 and add 4 gives 6 after 2; 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16 has differences 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 while doubling gives 8 after 4; jumped, played, walked, helped are regular and ran, went are the irregular past forms. The parameterised items were checked at the corners (d = 2..10, n = 1..5, a = 1..7, n = 2..6). Sequences and counting in steps match the UK national curriculum for Years 1 to 3.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets four documented slips. Copying the last item instead of finding the unit of repeat: the first gap rejects red with 'Not just the last one again'. Fixing a rule from the first two terms: testing Add 2 shows 4 → 6 ✗ against 8, and placing 10 says why. Being sure too early: in step 4 both rules fit 1, 2, 4, picking before the next number is refused, and the challenge 'enough' item repeats it with 3, 6. Overgeneralising a language rule: run + ed and go + ed show 'ran, not runned' and 'went, not goed', backed by mastery item m4.

lab_distinct.evidence: No other flagship lab tests competing rules against a sequence: here the learner fills gaps in a shape sequence and sees the unit of repeat bracketed, taps rule chips that mark each jump with a tick or cross, applies a suffix pattern to words and sees exceptions, reveals one more term to kill a rule, and builds a unit that the lab tiles across twelve slots. The 30% shingle gate passed against all other flagship labs, including flagplace and flaghelp.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea before the text names it: the bracket only appears once all three gaps are right, so the unit of repeat is seen; the cross under 4 → 6 shows that a rule must fit every jump; two of the six words refuse the -ed pattern, so the learner meets exceptions by trying; and the Double card turns red only when 7 is revealed, so the need for more evidence is felt. The free build step lets the child vary the unit length and see how many repeats fit in twelve.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the task then disproves: 'Red again, like the last one' (the gap rejects it), '10, because you add 2' (the rule test marks 4 → 6 with a cross), and '8, for sure: it doubles' (the next number is 7). The win message names the prediction and why the right answer holds.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating kinds (next shape, next number, size of the unit, enough evidence, -ed slip, why it works) with answer order rotated each round and fresh numbers for the step sequence. Each wrong option has its own message naming the slip: copied the last item, used a shape that is not in the pattern, skipped a place, assumed a jump of 1, doubled a step pattern, counted the whole row as the unit, was sure after two numbers, thought goed was right, or used the last jump only.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete examples a seven-year-old meets (red, blue, blue; 2, 4, 8, 16; jump, jumped; ran) and passed the kid FK limit in validate_lessons. Lab prompts are one or two short sentences, buttons are verb + object ('Test: Double', 'Put 16'). Adult text passed its limit and gives a concrete home routine with claps and cutlery.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph carries one idea (repeating unit, growing rule, test every jump and look for more, word patterns break). Each adult paragraph has one job: what the skill is and where the curriculum asks for it, the three habits, the named mistakes, and what to do at home. The lab has no decorative steps; every step adds one new habit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 375 px with touch: the ten-slot pattern wraps into rows of six and four so each unit bracket stays on one row, the four number boxes stay on one row with tick labels between them, word cards sit in two columns at 60 px tall, and every canvas action has a full-size button below. No control overflows the viewport and the walkthrough passed on the iPhone 13 profile.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin (add each shape, test each rule, put each number, word + ed, show the next number, pick a rule, clear). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the full sequence, the rule being tested and whether each jump fits; feedback and challenge results land in polite live regions. axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) reported no violations in light or dark theme on desktop and phone.
